title: Kernel scheduling + batching hackathon notes — PriorityWave experiment
body:
Context:
We ran a 24-hour internal hackathon (mini-sprint) to prototype a priority-aware scheduling layer for the serving runtime. Goal: reduce p95 latency for high-priority interactive requests while preserving aggregate throughput and keeping batching efficiency reasonable. The prototype is called "PriorityWave".

High-level idea:
- Tag incoming requests with priority buckets (P0, P1, P2) at the router level.
- Maintain separate fast-path micro-queues per priority and a background aggregator that opportunistically coalesces across buckets using a weighted coalescing window.
- Apply a tiny per-request deadline heuristic so that long-lived low-priority requests don't block high-priority waves.

What we implemented during the hackathon:
- Kernel-side change: added a new scheduling hook in the kernel's queue-manager that can preempt micro-batches if a P0 wave arrives and predicted completion for current batch > 12 ms. (See PR linked above.)
- KV cache integration: on P0 arrivals, we attempt a KV-prefetch refresher for the next 8 token steps if cache hit-rate for that client is > 60% (configurable). Prefetch runs async to avoid blocking.
- Batching heuristics: introduced adaptive budging window that grows/shrinks by +/- 1 token based on recent burstiness; budging window has an upper cap to avoid excessive wait.
- Observability: quick dashboards for p50/p95/p99 by priority, batch size distribution, and KV-prefetch success rate.

Key results from the 6-hour run against synthetic mixed workload (80% P2 background, 15% P1, 5% P0):
- P0 p95 latency: down 28% (from ~44ms to ~31.6ms)
- Aggregate tokens/sec: -3.4% (acceptable tradeoff in this patch experiment)
- Average batch size: down from 12.1 -> 9.0 (P0 bias reduced batch packing)
- KV-prefetch hit-rate improved for P0 by ~9 percentage points (async prefetch helped warm small session contexts)
- Observed jitter for P1 increased slightly (p95 +6%), likely due to interleaving preemptions

Notes / observations:
- Preempting long micro-batches helps interactive tails but reduces batch efficiency; the small aggregate TPS drop is in line with expectations for 5% high-priority traffic.
- Prefetch strategy helped short-lived sessions more than long-running chat sessions; tune threshold and lookahead window per customer class.
- We saw two kernel-edge race conditions where a preempt event and KV-prefetch callback contended for the same token-cache region. Patch included a lightweight spin-protected flag to mitigate (needs formal review).
- The weighted coalescing window works but has edge cases when priorities change mid-batch; need to handle priority escalation (P2 -> P0) without dropping in-flight tokens.

Open issues / blockers:
- RD-1298: formalize preempt rate limits (no more than X preempts/sec per device) — affects throughput SLAs.
- Need a plan for telemetry tagging to avoid high-cardinality explosion when we add priority + client id + model variant.
- Race condition with KV-prefetch callback under high concurrency (intermittent segfault in dev cluster). Repro steps added in Linear ticket.

Decisions made in hackathon:
- Keep preempt threshold conservative for now: kernel will only preempt if predicted remaining batch time > 12ms and at least 2 P0 requests are pending. This prevents noisy single-request preempts.
- Enable async KV-prefetch only for sessions with 3+ recent requests (simple LRU session counter) to avoid wasting memory bandwidth on cold sessions.

Action items (owners + ETA):
- Arjun: Harden kernel preempt hooks, add unit tests around preempt/rollback (ETA: 2027-07-14).
- Lena: Investigate segfault stacktrace from prefetchtask (ETA: 2027-07-09).
- Diego: Run 24-hour soak with mixed production traces and collect p50/p95 per-priority + batch-size distribution (ETA: 2027-07-13).
- Priya: Design telemetry label schema to limit cardinality; propose sampling rules (ETA: 2027-07-12).
- Maya: Draft rollout plan for canary (small subset of prod devices, opt-in customers) and prepare feature flag gate (ETA: 2027-07-15).

Quick experiments to try next sprint:
- Try relaxed preempt policy when global load < 60% to reclaim some throughput (adaptive preempting).
- Per-customer priority profiles: enterprise customers may buy guaranteed P0 fraction — model this in simulator.
- Combine KV-prefetch with cheap content hashing to detect session-state stability and avoid prefetching across noisy sessions.

Meeting notes from sync (2027-07-06 10:30 PT):
- Consensus to prioritize kernel correctness and telemetry before broad rollout.
- Agreed to run soak in staging with production traces rather than synthetic. Diego to coordinate with SRE for cluster reservation.
- No immediate API changes; router will add priority header but default behavior remains backward-compatible.

Misc (notes-to-self / scribbles):
- Try metric: "effective-batches-per-second" = total_batches / second weighted by priority
- Consider adding a KV-prefetch budget meter per-device to avoid network saturation on cold-start storms
- Remember: test multi-model serving path; current prototype tested only on 1 model type (Llama-3 variant).

Appendix: quick config knobs we used in prototype:
- preempt_time_threshold_ms = 12
- min_pending_for_preempt = 2
- kv_prefetch_lookahead = 8 tokens
- session_warm_count = 3
- budging_window_cap = 16 tokens

If you want to iterate on this: read the PR and the reproducer in RD-1298, ping me in #serving-runtime and we can triage the segfault together.

---
End of hackathon notes.
